commitResults.messageTitle: Reject too-long addresses when loading data
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonAdaptedPerson only checks that a saved address is not blank. The
Address constructor also rejects addresses longer than 105 characters,
but throws an IllegalArgumentException, which is not caught. As a
result, a data file with a too-long address crashes the app on start.

Check the length too and throw an IllegalValueException, so that the
data file is handled like any other invalid data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add VersionedAddressBook to keep a history
commitResults.messageBody:
An undo command needs to restore the contact list to an earlier state,
but AddressBook only holds the current data.

Let's add VersionedAddressBook, which saves a copy of the data on each
commit and can move back to the previous copy.

A commit is skipped when the data has not changed, so commands that do
not change the contact list leave no state behind.

Users cannot reverse a change made by mistake, such as deleting the
wrong contact.

Let's add an undo command that restores the contact list to its state
before the last change and shows all contacts.

LogicManager commits the address book after every command, so new
commands that change the contact list can be undone without extra
code. Commands that do not change the contact list are skipped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document undo command in user guide
Tidy up undo code and tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Some lines in the undo code and tests are longer than the soft limit of
110 characters, two test names do not follow the naming convention, and
VersionedAddressBook does not check that its state pointer stays valid.

Let's wrap the long lines, rename the tests and add assertions on the
state pointer.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort initial data before saving first state
commitResults.messageBody:
ModelManager saves the data it is given as the first undo state without
sorting it. If a pinned contact comes after an unpinned one in the data
file, undoing back to the first state sorts the contacts, so the commit
after the undo sees a change and saves an extra state.

Let's sort the initial data before saving it as the first state, so
that every saved state is in the order that is displayed.

The LogicManager test for undo only covers a single add command, so it
does not show that each kind of change is saved and undone in order.

Let's add a test that runs add, edit, pin, delete, list and clear, then
undoes them one at a time and checks the contacts after each undo.
